correctness.rationale: For every a≥2 and every multiplicative subgroup H≤(Z/2^aZ)^×, G=⟨−1⟩×⟨5⟩, ν_2(5^(2^k)−1)=k+2. Subgroups not containing −1 inject into the cyclic 5-power factor and hence are either U_j=units congruent 1 mod L or signed graph V_j (j≥1), h=2^j, L=2^a/h. Explicit coset arithmetic progression sums give U_j defect h(r−L/2) for each odd r in [1,L−1]; for V_j the union of two disjoint progressions gives exactly L/4 defects −2^(a−1) and L/4 defects +2^(a−1). Cosets of −1-containing groups pair to zero. All noncentral defects are odd nonzero, so a centered coset exists exactly iff −1∈H; half-interval balance holds iff −1∈H or 1+2^(a−1)∈H. Boundary a=2 and j=0 handled. Independently enumerated 2000 exact cosets for a=2..9 with zero discrepancies; all-a proof is group-theoretic and arithmetic.

value.rationale: Centered residue sums and half-interval balance are natural but inequivalent subgroup/coset invariants. The full signed/unsigned defect distributions close the 2-power modulus case neglected by odd-semiprime residue-sum work; exact multiplicities and the m=16 counterexample separate two established balance notions. The explicit all-subgroup classification is more informative than standard dyadic group structure alone, albeit elementary.

limitations: Only multiplicative cosets of unit subgroups modulo powers of two and first centered moments. Not arbitrary even composites, additive cosets, higher moments or incomplete residue sums.
